```text
1	# Live ASR with Sherpa-ONNX
2	
3	*Minimal, light, live speech recognition (and others) on Laptop's CPU*
4	
5	A terminal-based Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) application built with [Sherpa-ONNX](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx). Transcribe speech in real-time from your microphone or offline from WAV files — no GPU required. It also support diarization, TTS, and speech segmentation.  
6	
7	Documentation:  [![Ask DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/badge.svg)](https://deepwiki.com/bagustris/live-asr-sherpa).
8	
9	## Features
10	
11	- **Real-time microphone transcription** — partial hypotheses update live with <500 ms latency
12	- **Offline WAV transcription** — process audio files through the same pipeline
13	- **Speaker diarization** — colour-coded per-speaker output; ASR and diarization run concurrently to keep latency low
14	- **Unified model loading** — all sherpa-onnx model families supported via a single `--model-type` flag
15	- **CPU-optimized** — runs efficiently on any modern CPU using ONNX Runtime
16	- **Auto model download** — fetches the default Zipformer model on first run; diarization models also auto-downloaded
17	- **Endpoint detection** — intelligently segments speech with configurable silence rules
18	- **Rich terminal output** — colour-coded speaker labels and styled status messages via the `rich` library
19	
20	## Prerequisites
21	
22	- Python 3.8+
23	- A working microphone (for `--mic` mode)
24	- Linux recommended (Ubuntu compatible)
25	
26	## Getting Started
27	
28	### 1. Install dependencies
29	
30	```bash
31	pip install -r requirements.txt
32	```
33	
34	> **Note:** `rich` is included as a dependency for styled terminal output.
35	
36	### 2. Run
37	
38	**Microphone mode** — stream and transcribe live audio:
39	
40	```bash
41	python3 sherox/main.py --mic
42	```
43	
44	**WAV file mode** — transcribe a pre-recorded file:
45	
46	```bash
47	python3 sherox/main.py --wav path/to/audio.wav
48	```
49	
50	> [!NOTE]
51	> WAV files must be **mono, 16-bit, 16 kHz**. Convert with:
52	> ```bash
53	> ffmpeg -i input.wav -ar 16000 -ac 1 output.wav
54	> ```
55	
56	The default Zipformer model (~300 MB) is downloaded automatically on first run.
57	
58	## Speaker Diarization
59	
60	Add `--diarization` to any command to colour-code the transcript by speaker. Two lightweight models are downloaded automatically on first use (~7 MB segmentation + ~23 MB embedding):
61	
62	```bash
63	# Offline with diarization (auto-downloads all models)
64	python3 src/main.py --mic --offline --diarization
65	
66	# If you know how many speakers will be present:
67	python3 src/main.py --mic --offline --diarization --num-speakers 2
68	
69	# WAV file with diarization
70	python3 src/main.py --wav meeting.wav --offline --diarization --num-speakers 3
71	```
72	
73	Each speaker's transcript is printed in a distinct colour:
74	
75	```
76	  [Speaker 00] Good morning everyone.
77	  [Speaker 01] Thanks for joining the call.
78	  [Speaker 00] Let's get started.
79	```
80	
81	Diarization and ASR run **concurrently** (using a background thread pool), so the combined latency is approximately `max(ASR_time, diarization_time)` rather than the sum.
82	
83	## Supported Models
84	
85	All models from the [Sherpa-ONNX model zoo](https://k2-fsa.github.io/sherpa/onnx/pretrained_models/) can be used. Download and extract a model into the `models/` directory, then pass the directory name via `--model-dir` and the architecture via `--model-type`.
86	
87	> [!TIP]
88	> Models marked **auto** are downloaded automatically on first run. All others must be downloaded manually from the [Sherpa-ONNX releases page](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx/releases/tag/asr-models).
89	
90	### Online (Streaming) Models
91	
92	Use these with the default pipeline (no `--offline` flag). They support real-time partial hypotheses.
93	
94	| Model | `--model-dir` | `--model-type` | Lang | Notes |
95	|-------|--------------|----------------|------|-------|
96	| Zipformer En 2023 | `models/zipformer-en-2023` | *(blank)* | en | Default; **auto-downloaded** |
97	| Zipformer En 2024 | `models/sherpa-onnx-streaming-zipformer-en-2024-02-13` | `zipformer2` | en | Newer, slightly higher accuracy |
98	| Conformer En | `models/sherpa-onnx-streaming-conformer-en-2023-05-09` | `conformer` | en | Conformer transducer |
99	| Zipformer ZH/EN | `models/sherpa-onnx-streaming-zipformer-bilingual-zh-en-2023-02-20` | `zipformer` | zh/en | Bilingual |
100	| Paraformer ZH/EN | `models/sherpa-onnx-streaming-paraformer-bilingual-zh-en` | `paraformer` | zh/en | Streaming paraformer |
101	| WeNet CTC En | `models/sherpa-onnx-streaming-wenet-librispeech` | `wenet_ctc` | en | WeNet CTC |
102	| Zipformer2 CTC En | `models/sherpa-onnx-streaming-zipformer2-ctc-2024-09-18` | `zipformer2_ctc` | en | CTC variant |
103	
104	Example:
105	```bash
106	python3 src/main.py --mic \
107	  --model-dir models/sherpa-onnx-streaming-zipformer-en-2024-02-13 \
108	  --model-type zipformer2
109	```
110	
111	### Offline Models
112	
113	Use these with `--offline`. Audio is VAD-segmented before recognition (higher accuracy, higher latency). A [Silero VAD](https://github.com/snakers4/silero-vad) model (`silero_vad.onnx`) is auto-downloaded when needed.
114	
115	| Model | `--model-dir` | `--model-type` | Lang | Notes |
116	|-------|--------------|----------------|------|-------|
117	| Parakeet TDT 0.6B FP16 | `models/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2` | `nemo_transducer` | en | **Auto-downloaded** (`--offline` default) |
118	| Parakeet TDT 0.6B INT8 | `models/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2-int8` | `nemo_transducer` | en | **Auto-downloaded**; smaller & faster |
119	| Whisper tiny.en | `models/sherpa-onnx-whisper-tiny.en` | `whisper` | en | Smallest Whisper |
120	| Whisper base.en | `models/sherpa-onnx-whisper-base.en` | `whisper` | en | |
121	| Whisper small.en | `models/sherpa-onnx-whisper-small.en` | `whisper` | en | Good accuracy/speed balance |
122	| Whisper medium.en | `models/sherpa-onnx-whisper-medium.en` | `whisper` | en | Higher accuracy |
123	| Whisper large-v3 | `models/sherpa-onnx-whisper-large-v3` | `whisper` | multi | Multilingual; use `--language` |
124	| Paraformer ZH | `models/sherpa-onnx-paraformer-zh-2023-09-14` | `paraformer` | zh | |
125	| NeMo CTC En | `models/sherpa-onnx-nemo-ctc-en-conformer-medium` | `nemo_ctc` | en | NeMo Conformer CTC |
126	| SenseVoice | `models/sherpa-onnx-sense-voice-zh-en-ja-ko-yue-2024-07-17` | `sense_voice` | multi | 5 languages; use `--language` |
127	| Moonshine tiny | `models/sherpa-onnx-moonshine-tiny-en-int8` | `moonshine` | en | Very fast, English only |
128	| Moonshine base | `models/sherpa-onnx-moonshine-base-en-int8` | `moonshine` | en | Better accuracy than tiny |
129	| FireRedASR | `models/sherpa-onnx-fire-red-asr-large-zh-2025-02-16` | `fire_red_asr` | zh | |
130	
131	Examples:
132	```bash
133	# Parakeet TDT (auto-downloaded offline default)
134	python3 src/main.py --mic --offline --model-type nemo_transducer
135	
136	# Parakeet TDT INT8 (smaller, auto-downloaded)
137	python3 src/main.py --mic --offline \
138	  --model-dir models/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2-int8 \
139	  --model-type nemo_transducer
140	
141	# Whisper small (English)
142	python3 src/main.py --mic --offline \
143	  --model-dir models/sherpa-onnx-whisper-small.en \
144	  --model-type whisper
145	
146	# Whisper large-v3 (multilingual)
147	python3 src/main.py --mic --offline \
148	  --model-dir models/sherpa-onnx-whisper-large-v3 \
149	  --model-type whisper --language zh
150	
151	# SenseVoice (5 languages)
152	python3 src/main.py --mic --offline \
153	  --model-dir models/sherpa-onnx-sense-voice-zh-en-ja-ko-yue-2024-07-17 \
154	  --model-type sense_voice --language ja
155	
156	# Moonshine tiny
157	python3 src/main.py --mic --offline \
158	  --model-dir models/sherpa-onnx-moonshine-tiny-en-int8 \
159	  --model-type moonshine
160	```
161	
162	## CLI Options
163	
164	```
165	--mic                   Stream from microphone
166	--wav PATH              Transcribe a WAV file
167	--model-dir PATH        Sherpa-ONNX model directory
168	                          Default (online):  models/zipformer-en-2023
169	                          Default (offline): models/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2
170	--model-type TYPE       Model architecture hint (leave blank for auto-detect)
171	                          Online:  transducer, zipformer, zipformer2, conformer, lstm,
172	                                   paraformer, ctc, wenet_ctc, zipformer2_ctc
173	                          Offline: transducer, nemo_transducer, paraformer, whisper,
174	                                   ctc, nemo_ctc, sense_voice, moonshine, fire_red_asr
175	--offline               Use VAD-segmented offline pipeline instead of streaming
176	--language LANG         Language code for Whisper / SenseVoice (default: en)
177	--sample-rate INT       Audio sample rate in Hz (default: 16000)
178	--chunk-size FLOAT      Chunk size in seconds (default: 0.16)
179	--threads INT           CPU thread count for ONNX runtime (default: 4)
180	--capture-rate HZ       Microphone capture rate — use 48000 for device compatibility
181	--vad-model PATH        Path to silero_vad.onnx (auto-downloaded if not provided)
182	--listening             Show a live RMS energy bar for mic level calibration
183	--diarization           Enable speaker diarization with colour-coded output
184	--num-speakers N        Number of speakers (-1 = auto-detect, default: -1)
185	--diarization-seg-model PATH
186	                        Pyannote segmentation model.onnx (auto-downloaded if absent)
187	--diarization-emb-model PATH
188	                        Speaker embedding extractor .onnx (auto-downloaded if absent)
189	```
190	
191	## Architecture
192	
193	```
194	src/
195	├── main.py            # CLI entry point, model download, validation
196	├── asr_engine.py      # Unified model loading for all sherpa-onnx model types + diarization
197	├── streaming.py       # Streaming decode loop & VAD-segmented offline loop; rich output
198	├── audio.py           # Microphone capture & WAV file reading
199	├── config.py          # Configuration dataclass
200	└── requirements.txt   # Python dependencies
201	```
202	
203	| Module | Responsibility |
204	|--------|----------------|
205	| `main.py` | Parses arguments, validates inputs, auto-downloads model/VAD/diarization models, dispatches to streaming |
206	| `asr_engine.py` | Builds `OnlineRecognizer`, `OfflineRecognizer`, `VoiceActivityDetector`, or `OfflineSpeakerDiarization` |
207	| `streaming.py` | Feeds audio chunks to the recognizer; runs ASR and diarization concurrently; renders colour-coded output via `rich` |
208	| `audio.py` | Provides two generators: `mic_stream()` for live capture, `read_wav()` for file input |
209	| `config.py` | Holds runtime parameters (sample rate, chunk size, thread count, model path, language, diarization settings) |
210	
211	## Endpoint Detection (Online Mode)
212	
213	| Rule | Behavior |
214	|------|----------|
215	| Rule 1 | 2.4 s trailing silence → hard endpoint |
216	| Rule 2 | 1.2 s silence after sufficient speech → early endpoint |
217	| Rule 3 | 300 s max utterance → forced endpoint (effectively disabled) |
218
```
